thread:
elaine: Heads-up — started seeing 99th pct latency jump on model-cc-1024 around 11:07 UTC, coincides with the runtime rollout.
mike: Noted. Is this across all zones or a single host pool?
jana: I'm seeing it on gpupool-a (west). Throughput also dipped ~30%.
pranav: Any quick correlates from tracing? model, seq_len, or batch size?
elaine: Traces show requests spiking at seq_len=1024 and heavy tail for token gen. Kernel selector logs mention FlashAttn v2 fallback to a slower kernel for certain shapes.
elaine: deploy-bot: rolled out runtime/3.2.1 with triton_auto_kernel=true at 11:05 UTC :rocket:
sre-bot: alert: latency-spike detected (service=model-serving, p99=1.9s -> 3.4s)
mike: If triton_auto_kernel flipped, selector might've picked a new FlashAttn kernel that's slower on driver 535.x. We saw similar on small batches before.
jana: I pulled a profile on one impacted host: nvprof shows increased L2 transactions and higher sm_efficiency drop during attention kernel.
pranav: Can you paste kernel selection lines from the runtime logs? small snippet is fine.
jana: ```
[11:05:02] kernel_selector: model-cc-1024: chosen_kernel=flashattn_v2_shape_1024
[11:05:02] kernel_selector: fallback=false
[11:05:02] triton: launching kernel flashattn_v2_shape_1024 grid=(128,1,1) block=(256,1,1)
[11:06:58] kernel_selector: observed high mem_bandwidth, switching heuristics
```
elaine: Also noticed KV-cache miss rates increased for warm sessions — seems like some requests lost prefix caching and went through longer compute path.
mike: That could amplify the latency because cache misses change seq_len distribution seen by kernels.
pranav: Quick test idea: force runtime to use legacy flashattn kernel for seq_len>=512 and see if p99 recovers. We can flip a knob on a canary pool.
elaine: Agreed. Spinning up a canary patch now. Patch: `runtime.config.triton.force_kernel_override = legacy_flashattn` on gpupool-a-canary.
deploy-bot: canary deploy started: runtime/3.2.1+canary at 11:20 UTC
jana: Canary results after 5 mins: p50/p95 unchanged, p99 dropped back to ~1.8s. Throughput back to expected.
mike: That strongly implicates the auto-selected v2 kernel + driver interaction. Could also be batching heuristics changed to favour larger packing, exposing a bad path.
pranav: Need root cause: is it kernel microbenchmark mismatch or a driver/CUDA scheduling regression? Let's collect CUPTI traces and kernel counters (sm_efficiency, pmc stalls, l2_hit/miss) for both kernels.
elaine: I'll grab CUPTI traces from two nodes (one impacted, one canary) and upload to /tmp/diag/174350.
jana: Also include batch histogram and KV-cache hit logs from the same interval. The runtime emits `cache_hit_rate` per worker in trace.
mike: Action items:
- pr1: pranaV run CUPTI + nvprof capture for both kernels (pranav)
- pr2: runtime team to add selector telemetry: why v2 was preferred (elaine)
- pr3: SRE to rollback auto-kernel switch until we validate (mike)
- pr4: open issue with Triton/FlashAttn upstream if mismatch found (jana)

pranav: I'll attach traces in ~30m.
elaine: I'll also add a short-term guard: if p99>2.5s for 5m, force legacy kernel per model.
mike: Good. Can we also confirm driver versions on the hosts? I suspect mixed 535 vs 535.54.1 causing perf delta.
jana: Hosts show driver 535.101 on impacted, canary is 535.41. Both are in the 535 family but micro-diffs matter.
pranav: If it's driver-sensitive, we should pin kernel selection by driver version until a fix.
elaine: For transparency, I'll post a short incident note to #incidents after we have CUPTI results.
pranav: Traces uploaded: /tmp/diag/174350/pranav_cupti.zip
pranav: Quick diff: v2 kernel has 2.3x higher L2 miss ratio and 1.6x higher global memory load latency on impacted host.
jana: That matches the sm_efficiency drop. Looks like v2 exposes a memory access pattern that interacts poorly with this driver/hardware combo.
mike: Next: reproduce in a microbenchmark to validate and capture minimal repro. If repro is good, file bug with FlashAttn/Triton and upstream driver if needed.
elaine: SRE rolled back auto-kernel switch cluster-wide at 12:05 UTC. Metrics are back to baseline.
sre-bot: deploy: rollback completed runtime/3.2.1 -> runtime/3.2.0 at 12:05 UTC
mike: I'll schedule a follow-up postmortem to cover selector heuristics and add a test for kernel-driver compatibility gating.
jana: Also let's add a telemetry alert: sudden increase in cache_miss_rate or selector_switch_rate => auto-rollback.
elaine: Thanks all — great fast triage. We'll keep thread updated when we have upstream bug numbers.
pranav: Filed issue #INF-1938 with trace links and microbench results.
elaine: Incident note: https://redwood.internal/incident/INF-1938 (draft)
mike: Closing loop after PR with selector guard lands. :thumbsup:
